messages:
lina: Noticing apiserver p95 climbing in sa-east1 since ~14:30, controller-manager reconcile latencies spiking and heapster errors showing etcd timeouts. Multiple leader changes in etcd around 1851239950-1851240000.
oscar: I can confirm. netstat shows lots of retransmits and some out-of-order acks between ctrl-plane peers. suspect asymmetric path after the maintenance window on the peering router.
priya: GPU provisioner is drowning. ~90 pods in Pending with "AttachVolume timeout" and "failed to allocate GPU" events. If controller-manager keeps requeueing, it will worsen.
lina: Can we reduce controller-manager parallelism to slow the flood while infra investigates? Also thinking about soft-failing new GPU claims with a fallback placement to us-central1 for critical jobs.
oscar: lowering concurrency now: `kubectl -n kube-system patch deploy kube-controller-manager -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-controller-manager","args":["--concurrent-deployment-syncs=2","--concurrent-replicaset-syncs=2","--concurrent-service-syncs=1"]}]}}}}'`
devops-bot: patch applied by oscar at 1851240020.
priya: started tagging non-essential GPU workloads with `slo=best-effort` label; provisioner rule `prefer: us-central1 if slo=best-effort` will pick those up. preparing a rollback plan.
lina: good. oscar, can you run a quick tcpdump and paste sample? we need to show infra-net.
oscar: pasted excerpt:
```
14:31:12.001 IP sa-ctrl-a > internet-gw: IP frag 1/3 ...
14:31:12.002 IP internet-gw > sa-ctrl-a: ICMP unreachable, fragmentation needed and DF set
14:31:12.004 IP sa-ctrl-a > sa-ctrl-b: [RST]
14:31:12.210 IP sa-ctrl-a > sa-ctrl-b: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:31:12.412 IP sa-ctrl-b > sa-ctrl-a: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960
(retries)
```
priya: fragmentation/MTU mismatch could be killing some connections. that aligns with the ICMPs.
lina: infra-net, can you check peering MTU and any corridor changes? filing INF-9001.
sre-bot: ticket INF-9001 created and assigned to infra-net at 1851240065 by lina.
oscar: in the interim, i pushed placement rule: `k8s.provisioner/fallback=us-central1` for label `slo=best-effort`. Applied at 1851240080.
priya: metrics: apiserver_p95 dropped from 1.6s -> 700ms after concurrency change + initial fallback. pending GPUs down from 90 -> 34 in 6m.
lina: cost note: fallback to us-central will add ~0.08$/GPU-hour and ~0.02$/GB egress for some jobs. estimate ~80$/day if we keep current volume. logging to COST-ops.
oscar: infra-net responded: they saw a BGP maintenance flap that left one peering path with lowered MTU; rolling back the change now.
sre-bot: infra-net updated INF-9001: "peering config rollback started" at 1851240140.
priya: leader elections stopped after path recovered. controller-manager queue normalized. we'll keep the controller concurrency reduced for 15 more mins as a safety buffer.
lina: plan: 1) leave fallback rule for 30m, 2) create postmortem with timeline and cost impact, 3) follow up with infra-net for permanent fix (MTU mismatch guardrails). anyone object?
oscar: +1
priya: +1. I'll draft postmortem and include exact pod lists that were redirected.
devops-bot: action: rollback-schedule controller-manager-parallelism -> default in 15m created by lina at 1851240165.
lina: thanks everyone. will update when postmortem draft ready. :thumbsup:
